title: Comparing cards with different reward currencies
notice: Synthetic and illustrative. Card names, facts, identifiers and field names are invented for this example. The live server's advertised schemas are authoritative.
demonstrates: The assistant explains request history before the first Rewardopedia call.
Different reward currencies are not treated as equal money.
An unknown fee stays unknown instead of becoming zero.
No universal winner is declared from one number.

steps.text: Compare the Example Travel Card and the Example Cash Card for me.

Before I use Rewardopedia: it keeps a sanitized history of each Rewardopedia request, including searches and comparisons, in your Rewardopedia account until you delete it. It saves facts you tell me, such as cards you hold, but I won't save anything you ask me not to. Both are shared across assistants connected to your account, and you can ask what is saved or ask me to forget it at any time.

earning: 2 Example Miles per $1 on travel booked directly with airlines

steps.text: Example Travel Card: $250 annual fee; earns 2 Example Miles per $1 on travel booked directly with airlines; foreign transaction fee unknown. Example Cash Card: no annual fee; 1.5% cash back on everything; 3% foreign transaction fee. Miles and cash back are different currencies, so the 2x and 1.5% figures are not directly comparable as money. Neither card is better overall: the cash card is simpler and has no annual fee, while the travel card may suit you if you book airline travel and value miles. Would you like me to check either card's full fee details?
